2014 study suggests that reading paper books vs e-books is better for you.
It's an interesting article but the conclussions seems misleading. I think it would be more accurate to say that reading books on electronics are more likely to promote bad reading habits.

I don't know if better. but both have advantages. A book can go anywhere, all you need is a little light. E-books can carry so many great works of literature, but they do run out of power. Its a balance folks. My preference is always a paper book. I enjoy the simplicity of it. Technology is amazing and certainly serves a purpose, but I can't help feeling there is something about flipping the pages, taking your time, making notes in the margins, giving a classic and beautifully made book to a friend or loved one; paper books will always have something that electronic novels can never obtain. What that is may be hard to define exactly, but many of us know paper books are special to our education as human beings and to our enjoyment of the vast catalog of human knowledge and art. Go to the library folks. Remember, books are our friends.

What is your favorite stout and what is your favorite pairing for it?
I Hereby unofficially declare this Stout Week.

Since my favorite is a local seasonal offering, I will have to go with my favorite that is readily available year-round. That would be Left Hand Brewing's Milk Stout. While some would protest that the Milk Stout Nitro by Left Hand is superior, I tend to enjoy the hefty CO2 bite of the original.

As far as pairing (assuming you discount consuming it alongside 5 more of the same) I enjoy it with toffee ice cream or sticky toffee pudding. I am a toffee addict.

I have to say i'm partial to The Abyss from the Dechutes Brewery. and i don't think i've enjoyed myself more than when i had it with a bacon cheeseburger with tons of caremelized onions.

as for a stout that isn't woefully stuck in portland i'll have a Left Hand Milk Stout any day, any time.
